AcePolicyGate.description:
How the ACE engine treated the call at the moment a policy run completed.

`PolicyEngine.run` emits the SAME `PolicyRunComplete`, with the same
fields, whether (a) the policy chain was EMPTY and the target default
allowed, (b) a policy returned `Allowed`, or (c) every policy returned
`Continue` and the default allowed. So the event proves the target was
attached, `run` was called, and the call was not rejected — it does NOT
prove that any policy evaluated anything. Without this field the three
collapse onto one "a policy run exists" label, and a fail-open gate reads
as screened.

The vocabulary is deliberately the one the router provisioner already uses
for the same question (`workspace_routers::onchain::AceEntryGate`), minus
`Refused`: a refused call reverts and emits no `PolicyRunComplete`, so it
is structurally impossible for a RECORDED run and is not representable
here by construction.

PMM RFQ) | `bopamm` (Bebop BopAMM). Read from the handoff persisted for the leg,
so it is absent until the venue firmed it and on every non-RFQ leg. An open set:
a client renders an unknown value generically.

status.description: Leg status: `pending` | `executing` | `done` | `failed` | `refunded`.

oneOf.description:
The money-movement facts of a hosted venue trade's leg: a
payout or pay-in over a bank rail or a chain. Absent on route legs.

transactions.description:
The transactions this leg produced (a subset of the order's `transactions[]`,
correlated by `leg_index`/chain), each already enriched with an explorer URL.

venueRouteId.description:
The venue route identity that filled this leg, from the retained route quote's
`legQuotes[].solverId`. A solver-LP leg carries a real solver id that
resolves to a KYB'd LP workspace; a bridge leg carries a synthetic id
(e.g. `"circle-cctp"`) with no LP workspace behind it. This is the handle
the trade-detail builder uses to resolve per-leg counterparty compliance.

The selected funding wallet's balance of the quote's input token on its
source chain, read by this preflight. Absent for quotes whose input is not
an on-chain EVM token. A failed read is `unavailable`, never zero.

custodySigningError.description:
Operator-/user-facing failure reason when `custody_signing_status` is
`failed` / `failed_unreachable`; absent otherwise. Same handler-populated,
orders-row-sourced projection as `custody_signing_status`.

custodySigningStatus.description:
Custody-signing lifecycle status for backend-signed (Fireblocks / BitGo /
DFNS / Copper) orders, mirroring the durable `orders.custody_signing_status`
column (migration 187): `pending` (submitted to the provider, awaiting the
async signature), `signed`, `failed`, or `failed_unreachable` (no webhook
or reconciliation-poll response inside the sweep window). OMITTED for
non-custody orders (the column's `none` default) so their responses stay
byte-identical. Populated by the API handler from the orders row — the pure
`Order` conversion cannot read the DB and leaves it `None`.

custodyVaultAddress.description: Custody vault that signed a backend-signed order (`orders.custody_vault_address`).

deliveredOutputAmount.description:
What the settlement evidence says was ACTUALLY delivered, in the output
asset's base units.

`outputAmounts` above is the quote's commitment and says so; until this
field existed its doc comment could only point clients at "terminal
transaction, settlement/provider, and balance evidence", i.e. at work
the backend had already done. `lifecycle::apply_transition` captures the
delivered amount on the settle transition and `orders` stores it; every
consumer of this DTO was simply unable to read it.

Absent when nothing has been captured yet — an order that has not
settled, or a durable row written before the capture existed. Never
guessed from the quote: the quote-carried case is reported honestly by
`deliveredOutputProvenance`.

deliveredOutputProvenance.description:
Where `deliveredOutputAmount` came from: `"measured"` when it was read
back from settlement evidence (a receipt-backed bridge delivery, a
realized DEX output, a Circle-settled FX output, a deferred settlement's
executed amount), `"quoted"` when a quote-time value was carried forward
because nothing measured the delivery.

This field is the whole point of the pair. The lifecycle falls back to
the quoted output when no measurement exists, which makes "measured,
zero slippage" and "never measured" byte-identical — `realizedSlippageBps`
reads 0 for both and the delivered column repeats the quote. A client
that renders a delivered amount without reading this is reporting a
quote as a receipt.

directUserId.description: Broker-onboarded direct user this order was submitted for.

executionDeadlineAt.description:
Deadline by which execution had to complete before the TTL watchdog
marks the order expired (`orders.execution_deadline_at`).

executionDeadlineKind.description:
Why `executionDeadlineAt` exists: `enforced` (configured SLA) or the
product default (`orders.execution_deadline_kind`).

oneOf.description: Structured failure details when status is failed.

feeUsd.description: Total fee paid by the user in USD (`orders.fee_usd`).

filledAt.description: When the fill transaction was observed (`orders.filled_at`).

legAttempts.description:
Ended attempts per leg of a multi-leg route, keyed by leg index. The attempt in
progress is the number of ended attempts plus one. Absent until a leg has ended
an attempt.

legs.description:
Uniform per-leg execution model for multi-leg route orders (li.fi-style
`includedSteps`). Absent for single-leg escrow / deferred orders, whose
`transactions[]` timeline is the whole story. Leg status is projected from
the route cursor and can temporarily trail a mined transaction; correlate
it with `transactions[]` and provider references before treating `pending`
as evidence that execution did not occur.

oneOf.description: The same server-owned lifecycle status the trade list carries.

linkedWalletId.description: Linked wallet used for settlement (None for legacy orders).

oneOf.description:
What this multi-leg order needs from its reader next: sign the next leg, accept a
moved price, retry a leg that did not run, finish the trade, or nothing because it
stopped or is under review. Absent when nothing is needed. Computed by the backend
from the route's durable state; clients switch on `kind` and never infer it from
`substatus`, which keeps its own meaning.

nextActions.description:
Follow-up signed actions the client must perform after submit (e.g. the
Circle StableFX Permit2 funding signature). Empty for single-step orders.
Terminal orders and consumed or expired composite permits expose no action.
Clients must still submit the exact permit and retain it for idempotent retries.

oneOf.description: Who must act next, including follow-up signatures visible only on the order read.

orderKind.description:
Canonical, route-aware order kind for status/history + SDK clients
(`cctp-v0` / `across-v4` / `relay-v0` / `fx-v0` / `composite-v0` / `escrow-v0` /
`deferred` / …). Always present. Prefer this over `order_type`, which collapses
routes to `generic-v0`. See [`crate::orders::Order::order_kind`].

outputAmounts.description:
Output amounts committed by the accepted quote/order. These are not an
execution receipt and may differ from the ultimately delivered balance
after venue fees or permitted price movement; use terminal transaction,
settlement/provider, and balance evidence for actual delivery.

pairQuoteId.description:
The held pair-quote id (`q_…`) the order was placed by (`POST /orders {quoteId}`):
the id Review and the quote card showed. `quoteId` above stays the internal route or
solver quote it executed. Recorded server-side from the held quote, never from the
request; absent for orders placed with a full quote body and for orders placed before
it was recorded.

realizedSlippageBps.description:
Realized adverse slippage in basis points, computed at settlement as
`10000 * (quoted_output - delivered_output) / quoted_output`. Negative
means the delivery beat the quote.

Deliberately NOT named `slippageBps`: this struct already carries
`slippageToleranceBps`, which is the tolerance the order was SUBMITTED
with — a quote-time input, not an outcome. Two fields one word apart
that mean "what I allowed" and "what I got" is how a caller ends up
charting the limit as the result, so the outcome names itself.

Only meaningful alongside `deliveredOutputProvenance == "measured"`; a
`"quoted"` provenance makes this structurally 0.

recipientAddress.description:
Wallet that receives the output: the fill's recipient when known, else
the signed intent / route preview receiver. A workspace-router proxy is
reported as-is; it forwards to the taker at settlement.

oneOf.description: Optional reporting guidance; never changes order execution status.

route.description:
Resolved display identity for the order's primary input/output leg:
symbol, name, decimals, chain id + chain ref, and the amount already
scaled by those decimals (`decimalAmount`).

This exists because `inputAmounts`/`outputAmounts` carry only a raw
`AssetRef` + base-unit integer, and the metadata needed to interpret
them lives in the backend's registry-derived catalogue — a client that
cannot find the token has no way to scale the number and ends up
printing base units as a human quantity (a Solana leg rendered
`940,000` for 0.94 PYUSD). `resolutionStatus` states honestly whether
the backend resolved the asset; when it is `unknown`, `decimals` and
`decimalAmount` are absent rather than guessed.

Purely additive: `inputAmounts`/`outputAmounts` are unchanged, and
`rawAmount` here repeats their value verbatim. Always serialized;
`#[serde(default)]` only so a stored payload written before this field
existed still deserializes.

senderAddress.description:
Wallet that funds the order: the signed intent's depositor (escrow /
eip3009 message `sponsor` / `user` / `signer` / `from`), the route
preview's input owner, or the StableFX taker. Handler-populated from
the durable row; absent when nothing recorded it.

settlementSpeedMs.description: `settled_at - created_at` in milliseconds, captured at settlement.

slippageToleranceBps.description:
Client-selected slippage tolerance in basis points: the deferred/OTC submit
tolerance, or for a multi-leg route the tolerance each continuation re-quote may
absorb (the quote request's `intent.metadata.allowedSlippageBps`, default 30).

status.description:
Coarse current status of the order. Terminality is order-kind dependent:
route and atomic venue orders normally complete at `settled`, while
claim-based or deferred products may continue to `finalized`. Use
`substatus` for the route/provider state and do not wait for `finalized`
unconditionally.

stuckSince.description: Last update of a nonterminal order that is stuck waiting on its counterparty.

substatus.description:
Finer-grained state within `status`, when one applies. Route orders surface the
`routeStatus` (`bridging` / `arrived` / `manualReview` / …); escrow/deferred
orders surface the fine wire states the coarse `status` hides (`postFilled` / …).

substatusCode.description:
Machine-readable reason for the current `substatus`, when the client needs
to choose a recovery action without parsing `substatusMessage`.

substatusMessage.description: Human-readable elaboration of `substatus` (e.g. a Circle StableFX status line).

terminal.description:
Whether the order lifecycle is terminal and cannot advance any further.
This is computed by the backend from the product-specific state machine;
clients should poll this field instead of inferring terminality from the
coarse `status` or `substatus` vocabulary.

transactions.description:
Best-effort transaction references for observed lifecycle stages, enriched at
serve time with `label` + `explorerUrl` + `legIndex`. Projection can lag the
chain/provider; absence is not proof that no transaction was submitted.

OrderTransactionInfo.description:
Transaction reference for an order lifecycle stage.

The trailing `leg_index` / `label` / `explorer_url` fields are additive,
serialize-skipped when `None`, and populated only at response-projection time
(never by observers / storage / adapters), so every internal construction site
leaves them `None`. They enrich the wire timeline for programmatic (SDK) consumers:
which route leg a tx belongs to, a human role label, and a ready-to-open explorer URL.

explorerUrl.description:
Block-explorer URL for `hash` on `chain_id` when the backend maps the chain;
`None` → the client falls back to its own per-chain explorer registry.

label.description:
Human-friendly role label (e.g. "Bridge burn", "Fill", "Claim"); when `None`
the client derives it from `stage`.

legIndex.description: 0-indexed route leg this tx belongs to (multi-leg routes only).

timestamp.description:
Unix seconds at which the platform OBSERVED this transaction — the wall clock
of the observer that recorded it, never the block time (no observer reads one).

`None` means the row was DERIVED at serve time from a `settlement.data` hash
reference whose observation was never stamped, so this build genuinely does not
know when the transaction happened. It is deliberately absent rather than filled
with the enclosing order's `updated_at`: that value is not this transaction's
time, it renders as a plausible one, and it advances on every later order write —
so the timeline both inverted causality (a fill dated after the bridge burn it
funded) and moved between two reads of the same immutable transaction. A client
must render "time unknown" for `None`, never substitute one of its own.

Order lifecycle stage that a transaction belongs to.

basis.description: Where the price came from: a live venue quote, published levels, or a model.

commitment.description:
`indicative` (a price, never orderable except through its `next: order`, executed within the caller's
minimum receive) or `executable` (`firm`: the venue is bound; otherwise held to `minOut`).

corridors.description: The venue's other supported corridors; changing one is a Requote.

expiresAt.description: When an executable quote stops being orderable; null for an indicative one (see `staleAfter`).

fees.description:
Every fee line, its payer and whether `receive.amount` already includes it; an amount that could
not be read is null, never 0.

oneOf.description:
When this card's venue gives its binding price, from the venue's own declaration:
`onRequest` (a desk is firm-asked by Get firm quote or a requote) or `atExecution`
(the venue prices firm only when the order executes, so Get firm quote is not offered).
Absent when no venue declares it (protocol routes, order books, fiat venues).

firmAskAvailableAt.description:
When this desk takes its next firm ask: its firm-quote limit for this workspace is reached
until then, so Get firm quote and an order-time ask are refused before it. Absent
when no limit is known here; the desk's admission still decides at ask time.

oneOf.description: Current workspace/venue firm asks, read without contacting the provider.

id.description:
The held quote's id (`q_` + ULID): order it with `POST /orders {quoteId}`, preflight it with
`POST /orders/preflight {quoteId}`, requote it with `POST /quotes {requote: id}`. It belongs to the
principal that asked; another principal reads it as unknown (404).

legs.description:
One leg per venue the quote runs through, in execution order: a multi-leg route (for example
CCTP then Circle StableFX) lists each leg's venue and location.

oneOf.description:
The most `pay.amount` a `receiveExact` venue card may debit: the mirror of `minOut`, the quoted
debit grown by `priceProtectionBps`. It is the consent an order on it carries, so Confirm's
one fresh quote of an expired card is judged by it. Absent for `payExact`.
The native mechanism that actually supplied this venue's price.
The least `receive.amount` execution may deliver (from `priceProtectionBps`).

netReceived.description:
`receive.amount` minus every other cost, converted at the Reference mid: for
comparison and sort only, never what lands.

next.description:
The caller's next call: `preflight` (protocol), `order`, `requote` (a production venue's indicative
card: its firm quote comes from a requote), or what to fix first.

observedAt.description:
When the price was observed: an indicative price, or the book read an executable
order-book estimate (one that reprices when chosen) was priced from; null for a firm quote.

pay.description: What the taker pays: Asset, chain (null off-chain), variant and amount in Asset units.

readiness.description: Whether the quote can be ordered now (funding, gas, wallet); an unknown is `unavailable`, never 0.

receive.description:
`receive.amount` is what lands at `deliverTo`, after every `included: true` fee
taken in the receive Asset.

refundClaimableAfter.description:
With `refundOnSource` on an escrowed intent: the instant after which the source-chain
escrow refunds the input if the order was not filled, read from the signed order's own
expiry (`expires`). Until then the input stays in that escrow. Absent when the quote holds
no escrowed intent or its expiry could not be read; never estimated.

requoteOf.description:
The quote this one requoted (`POST /quotes {requote}`); the original stays orderable until its own
expiry, and a route's requote is that same route.

retainUntil.description:
The last instant this held quote can still be requoted, or ordered where its lapse
allows it: its lapse plus the requote window (10 minutes), or the recovery window
(30 minutes) for a protocol quote. After it, requote and order answer 410
`QUOTE_EXPIRED`. Read from the held quote's own retention, never computed by a client;
absent when that instant is not representable.

signaturesRequired.description:
Every signature the order needs. `next.sign` carries the first; later ones arrive
on the order as `signNextLeg`.

spreadFromMidBps.description: The price's distance from the Reference mid, or the reason it is unknown.

staleAfter.description: When an indicative price goes stale; null for an executable quote.

oneOf.description:
What a `payExact` card leaves unspent of the amount asked: an order book fills whole
lots, so the card spends less and the rest stays where it is paid from. Absent when the card
spends the whole amount.

walletSelection.description: Why each Basic on-chain wallet was selected. Response metadata, never request authority.

propertyNames.description:
A CAIP-2 chain id (`eip155:8453`, `solana:<genesis>`, `tron:shasta`), syntax-checked:
a namespace of 3 to 8 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, and a reference of 1 to 32
letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Compared exactly, as CAIP-2 references are case-sensitive.

PairQuote.description:
One venue's quote for the pair. Every field is always present; one that does not
apply to the quote's commitment is `null`:

| field | indicative | executable, firm | executable, non-firm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expiresAt` | null | set | set |
| `minOut` | null | null | set |
| `observedAt`, `staleAfter` | set | null | null |

A stub (`sources[].priceOnRequest`) is indicative with `null` amounts.

The example is an executable non-firm quote: 10000 USDC paid,
`receive.amount` 9996.0 USDT lands after the included 4.0 USDT provider fee;
`netReceived` 9994.8 also subtracts the 0.0004 ETH network fee the taker pays
separately (`included: false`, about 1.2 USDT at the Reference mid), so it is lower
than `receive.amount`; `minOut` 9966.01 (30 bps) bounds `receive.amount`, not
`netReceived`.

is one of that account's linked wallets on the venue's network, and otherwise quotes from
its own default; a venue is never refused because of it. `bind.wallets` is the explicit
choice and wins on its chain.

details.description:
Requirement-specific facts; `details.reason` names why a blocked requirement is
blocked. A `ROUTE_EXECUTABLE` source signing window must leave at least the source
chain's relayer inclusion window (12 s on Base, OP, Robinhood and Arc testnet, 24 s
on Ethereum, 30 s on any other chain). Under it the reason names the deadline that
binds:
- `quoteLifeTooShort` `{remaining, required}` (ISO 8601 durations): the quote ends
  before the transaction can be included; `remediation` is `refreshQuotes`.
- `sourcePermitExpired` `{deadline}` (unix seconds): a bridge source permit ends
  before the quote does.

PriceRowStatus.description:
A row's outcome:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `priced` | a fresh cached price |
| `stale` | past `staleAfter`, or a private source still warming; any price kept |
| `unsupported` | `pairNotServed`: the venue holds nothing for the pair; `priceSourceNone`: it publishes no price (asked only on `POST /quotes`); `receiveExactUnsupported` |
| `belowMin` | the first size is under the source's minimum |
| `insufficientDepth` | the source cannot fill the first size |
| `needsWallet` | the venue prices only for a wallet |
| `restricted` | a gate keeps the desk price from this principal |
| `unavailable` | a read failed, or a fee could not be computed; `notYetPublished`: the venue publishes this pair and nothing is cached for it yet |

One requested size, with a quote's meanings: `receive` is what lands after every
`included` fee taken in the receive Asset, `netReceived` is for comparison only.

pay.description: The pay amount priced: the request's, rounded down to the source's precision.

oneOf.description: `null` when nothing could be priced at this size, never `0`.

PricesLadderLevel.description: One incremental level: `size` more pay units, each buying `price` receive units.

computedAt.description: When the server built this snapshot (it reuses one for about a second).

payBalances.description:
The pay Asset in the caller's own Default-binding wallets, one memory-only read
per deployment (only the pinned chain when `pay.chain` is set). Display only, never a
quote input. Empty for an API key, before the first warm, or with no bound wallet:
unknown, never zero. A client totals the `fresh` entries and names every other entry
as not read, never a silent partial total.

oneOf.description: The pair's indicative reference mid, from the same source as POST /quotes. null only when the read failed, with the cause in referenceMidUnavailable; never zero, stale or guessed. Never a quote input.

referenceMidUnavailable.description:
Why `referenceMid` is `null`: `marketDataUnavailable` (a market-data refusal or outage),
`notPriced` (no reference price exists for an asset) or `timedOut` (past the read's budget).

QuoteSourceEntry.description:
One considered venue's outcome, a closed set tagged `status`:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `asking` | in flight on the stream only: the auction is consulting this venue now; its final outcome replaces it under the same venue key, and none remains at `complete` |
| `answered` | the venue produced a quote |
| `needsWallet` | no wallet of `family` to ask with |
| `walletRefused` | the bound wallet is refused (`Revoked`, a confirmed sanctions hit) |
| `firmQuoteLimited` | a desk's firm-quote cap applies; `explanation` is product copy |
| `priceOnRequest` | no venue price was requested; `quoteId` identifies the held estimate or stub to Requote |
| `askLimitReached` | the venue's ask limit is reached for now; `retryAfter` says when to ask again |
| `timedOut` | no answer inside the deadline |
| `refused` | the venue refused the live ask |
| `restricted` | a gate kept the venue from this principal |
| `unsupported` | the venue does not serve the pair |
| `filteredOut` | the request's own filters exclude it (never a coverage or chain gap) |
| `unavailable` | a read failed (`kybUnavailable`, `admissionUnavailable`, …) |

An unscreened default wallet is not a status: the quote carries `screening`. `venue`
is the venue block, its `id` the one quote legs and `/prices` rows carry. Durations
(`retryAfter`) are ISO 8601, counted from when the response was sent. Every entry
carries `asked`: whether this venue was consulted for this request: a live ask, or a
fresh read of its published book or live desk price within that source's freshness
window. An estimate no venue gave (a model or reference price) is not consulted, and
an `answered` entry is always consulted. How a card's price was obtained is its own
price basis, never this flag.

Ask for the permission or wallet right `target`. For a member session it is offered only
when the permission-request owner would open (or already holds) a request on it; a target
it refuses by name (`blocked`, `not_applicable`, ...) reads `none`. When that read fails,
the step is offered unchanged.

The calling member's own pending request for this same target (the target key
the create route deduplicates on, so a request made from another venue's card
counts), read once per auction: the member already asked, so a client shows that
instead of offering a second request. Absent when there is none, when the read
failed or timed out (never a guessed value), and always for API keys and
automation principals: only a member session's quotes carry it.

post.description: Place an order by the id of a quote you hold (`{quoteId}` from POST /quotes). A venue (Basic) quote becomes a venue trade (`basicTrade`); a protocol (Advanced) quote becomes a protocol order (`advancedTrade`), after POST /orders/preflight and any wallet signature or source transaction it asks for. parameters.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for API keys (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED); optional for signed-in members. 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. post.description: The asset-pair contract (PairQuoteRequest or RequoteRequest); the legacy intent body is retired, so an object without `pay` or `requote` is 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming `pay`. Validated in order (INVALID_REQUEST naming the field, REQUOTE_FIELDS_CONFLICT, UNKNOWN_ASSET / UNKNOWN_CHAIN / UNKNOWN_VENUE naming the value, ASSET_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a side's Asset has no deployment on the chain pinned for it), INVALID_AMOUNT, SAME_ASSET_NEEDS_CHAIN, CHAIN_PIN_NEEDS_ON_CHAIN, out-of-range INVALID_REQUEST, ROUTING_OPTIONS_FORBIDDEN), then the request_quotes capability, and answered with a PairQuoteSet: every venue planned, venue-hitting plans limited to one every 3 s per principal (429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; cache-only plans are not limited), quotes held for their owner and the set recorded for GET /quotes/requests/{quoteRequestId}. A requote body asks only the earlier quote's venue again (every venue of a multi-leg route, which answers that same route), as JSON (never a stream), and answers a PairQuoteSet whose one quote names it in requoteOf; the earlier quote stays held until its own expiry. Requote refusals: 400 CORRIDOR_NOT_OFFERED / BINDING_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a custody vault or registered workspace address bound to a chain it is not an account of; also on a fresh request), 403 SOURCE_NOT_OWNED / ACCOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE / VENUE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIAL, 404 QUOTE_NOT_FOUND (unknown and another principal's quote alike), 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED (details.reason) / REQUOTE_NEEDS_WALLET / PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED / QUOTE_CANNOT_BE_REFRESHED (a quote recorded before it could be refreshed for a broker's client), 410 QUOTE_EXPIRED (10 minutes after its expiry), 429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED / FIRM_QUOTE_LIMITED / BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After, 503 QUOTE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE / QUOTE_NOT_READY, 504 REQUOTE_TIMED_OUT. Every refusal, at every status, is the one error body ApiError {error, message, requestId, timestamp, next?, details?}. Optional filters narrow the auction. Venue-account cards require a current MFA human Company/Broker session, or an API key holding workspace_venue_trade with its venue switch enabled and HMAC request signing; any other key's request still succeeds and lists the venue restricted (venueTradeScopeRequired). An API key quotes with quotes_request (which needs orders_write on the same key); it has no Default wallet of a member, so it binds a workspace wallet in bind.wallets: a workspace custody wallet, or an organisation wallet the key was granted (without that grant the source reads API_KEY_ORGANISATION_WALLET_SCOPE_REQUIRED), never a personal one (409 PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED); its protocol venues read needsWallet until it binds one. A desk on a production site is firm-asked only on request, the same for sessions and API keys, each one call: name it in filters.venues.include and its firm quote returns in that response, or requote its indicative card ({requote: quoteId}). A broad request never asks it: its card stays indicative and reads unavailable priceOnRequest when it publishes no price. Its next is requote, except where its firm quote lives 5 s or less: then it is order (execute within my limit), and that order makes the one ask, trading only at or above the person's minReceive; a requote of that card (Get firm quote) also asks it once under the same desk limits and returns a firm, executable card with its expiresAt. A sandbox or testnet desk that publishes nothing is firm-asked on a person's or API caller's request within the desk limits (firmQuoteLimited with retryAfter when they are reached); automation principals get it on requote only. On a venue-account card, bind.deliverTo {kind: address, chain, address, destinationTag?} names where the trade's output is withdrawn when the order for it fills: one of the workspace's own wallets that is an approved withdrawal destination of that venue account, for the receipt asset, with exactly that destination tag or memo. The card then carries that deliverTo, a network fee line for the venue's withdrawal fee (the most the order will pay; a higher fee at send refuses) and a receive net of it (netReceived unavailable withdrawalFeeUnread when the fee could not be read), and a requote keeps it. A venue that cannot deliver there answers its source unavailable with DESTINATION_NOT_APPROVED, DELIVER_TO_NOT_A_WORKSPACE_WALLET, WITHDRAWAL_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED (no withdrawal network for that chain on the site; test sites have none), DELIVER_TO_AMBIGUOUS, WITHDRAWAL_FEE_EXCEEDS_AMOUNT, deliverToCalldataUnsupported or deliverToNotPermitted (deliverTo needs a member session with ViewWallets; an API key lists no deliverTo candidates, and a requote naming one answers 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED with details.reason deliverToNotPermitted). The request spends one Quote token; connection indicative pacing is reported on cards.
